title: Quantization Certification Stamps and Sample-Replay Manual
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This page defines the certification "stamps" we apply to quantized model artifacts, the acceptance criteria for each stamp, and a reproducible sample-replay procedure used by model-onboarding, CI, and shadow-rollouts to validate quality and performance before traffic migration. This is intended for engineers and evaluators running quant migration for real-time and streaming services.

Goals and principles:
- Provide a compact, machine- and human-readable artifact certification that drives automated gating and manual signoffs.
- Ensure replayed samples exercise realistic runtime characteristics (KV cache, prefix-shared contexts, functioncall sequences).
- Keep safety and coherence prioritized: latency/throughput improvements may not compensate for unacceptable fidelity regressions.

Certification stamps (high-level):
1) GREEN (go): Quantized artifact meets fidelity, latency, and memory budgets for production; auto-promotable to Canary.
2) AMBER (guarded): Passes baseline runtime checks but exhibits marginal fidelity deltas on one or two slices; requires human review and mitigations (prompt rewrite, fallback policy).
3) RED (reject): Fails fidelity or functioncall correctness thresholds or shows catastrophic tokenization divergence; block rollout.
4) ORANGE-QUANT-SHADOW (experimental): For artifacts intended only for private/dedicated shadow with enabled quant-hedging and restricted tenant cohorts.

Stamp metadata (artifact manifest fields):
- artifact_id: unique artifact hash (SHA256).
- base_model: model family (e.g., redwood-mocha-7b).
- quant_profile: name (e.g., int4-hybrid-kv-preserve-v2).
- stamp: GREEN|AMBER|RED|ORANGE-QUANT-SHADOW.
- fidelity_delta_p95: string percentage (e.g., "0.8%") measured against baseline.
- latency_tail_ms_p99: numeric string (e.g., "42").
- evaluated_slices: comma-separated list (e.g., "fewshot-instr,code-gen,funcall").
- eval_run_id: internal job id.
- signer: team/person certifying.
(Include these fields in quant artifact JSON stored in the artifact registry.)

Acceptance criteria (concrete thresholds):
- Fidelity: end-to-end response similarity (ensembled F1/ROUGE-like anchor) delta p95 <= 1.5% for GREEN, <= 3.5% for AMBER. RED otherwise.
- Functioncall correctness: exact-match success rate >= 99% for GREEN, >= 97% for AMBER.
- Safety sentinels: zero high-severity safety sentinel hits in production-sim probe for GREEN; AMBER may have isolated low-severity hits with documented mitigations.
- Latency/Memory: p99 latency <= baseline_p99 * 1.15 for GREEN; p99 latency <= baseline_p99 * 1.40 for AMBER. Memory footprint within configured host OOM margin (artifact must report static-kv-size <= declared).
- Tokenization parity: token count delta <= 2 tokens on average for conversational probes.

Operational replay harness (overview):
The sample-replay harness runs a deterministic subset of probes through the quantized artifact under a runtime shim that reproduces production batching and KV-cache priming. It has three execution modes: local, CI, and shadow.

Required inputs:
- probe-bundle.tar.gz (contains 3k–10k probes, stratified by slice).
- artifact metadata JSON (artifact manifest above).
- runtime-config.yaml (serving flags: batch_window_ms, kv_cache_enabled=true/false, temperature, functioncall-mode).

Sample runtime-config.yaml example:
---
batch_window_ms: 10
kv_cache_enabled: true
max_sequence_len: 2048
temperature: 0.0
functioncall_mode: permissive
replay_workers: 8
max_concurrency: 64
---

Replay CLI (example):
# run locally against a runtime that exposes gRPC test-hook
replay-harness run --artifact /tmp/artifact.tar.gz --probes /tmp/probe-bundle.tar.gz --config runtime-config.yaml --out /tmp/replay-output --mode local

Important checks (automated):
- Response similarity metrics (anchored embeddings cosine, normalized edit distance) per slice.
- Functioncall token stream diff and JSON schema validation for all functioncall responses.
- Safety sentinel scan results (severity-coded).
- Latency and memory profile capturing: p50/p95/p99, ingestion-to-first-token, greedy vs streaming behavior.
- Token-level divergence heatmap for long-context tests (store histogram).

Pass/fail decision logic (CI):
1) Run replay in CI with --mode ci and 95% slice coverage.
2) If any RED criterion (functioncall < 97%, safety high-severity) -> fail and attach artifacts to ticket.
3) If within AMBER thresholds -> create rollout ticket assigned to owning squad; require human review and a targeted canary with quant-hedge enabled.
4) If GREEN -> annotate artifact with stamp=GREEN and allow Canary promotion pipeline to start automatically.

Manual review checklist for AMBER artifacts:
- Review top 20 probes with largest fidelity delta.
- Inspect failure modes: hallucination, length truncation, tokenization mismatch, numeric instability.
- Validate mitigations: prompt-slice rewrite, per-route fallback to base float model, functioncall schema enforcement.
- Decide on staged rollout plan and rollback criteria (explicit metric thresholds and time windows).

Telemetry and observability requirements (per artifact rollout):
- Instrument per-request: artifact_id, quant_profile, eval_run_id, response_similarity_score, kv_cache_hit, functioncall_ok.
- Set alerting: response_similarity_score p95 drop > 2% for production slices -> page SEV2; any safety high-severity -> SEV1.
- Retain replay-output bundles (including raw diffs) for 90 days for triage.

Rollback and fallback policies:
- Immediate fallback: runtime-side guard that detects functioncall schema errors or safety high-severity and routes requests to float fallback endpoint for the request.
- Canary-scale rollback: automated rollback if any of (response_similarity delta p95 > 3%, functioncall error rate increase > 1% absolute, consumer-telemetry error budget depletion > 25%) during canary window.
- Long-tail rollback: if after 72 hours secondary signals degrade (embedding drift, downstream rerank loss), schedule full rollback and postmortem.

Example artifact promotion flow (short):
1) Author attaches quant artifact and replay result to promotion PR.
2) CI runs harness; if GREEN, artifact stamped and PR merges.
3) Auto canary: 2% traffic for 1h with quant-hedge=50% (route 50% to base float if any marginal signal).
4) If canary healthy -> ramp to 25% for 6h -> full ramp over 24h.

Slicing strategy for probe bundles (recommended):
- Core slices: instruction-following, few-shot completion, functioncall sequences, code generation, multimodal priming (if applicable).
- Risk slices: numeric-precision, date-parsing, privacy triggers, regulatory prompts.
- Edge slices: long-context (>2048), adversarial prompt set, non-English samples.
- Each bundle must include traffic-weight annotations to compute weighted deltas.

Playbook: Quick-start run (engineer):
1) Fetch baseline float artifact and quant candidate from registry.
2) Generate probe-bundle via: probe-builder assemble --slices core,risk --seed 42 --size 5000 --out bundle.tar.gz
3) Prepare runtime-config.yaml per target deployment.
4) Run local replay: replay-harness run --artifact candidate.tar.gz --probes bundle.tar.gz --config runtime-config.yaml --mode local --out ./results
5) Inspect ./results/summary.json and top-deltas.csv. If GREEN, open a promotion PR.

Ownership and escalation:
- Artifact owner: model-onboarding team (primary), runtime-optimization (secondary).
- On-call escalation: quant-eval@redwood for AMBER/RED anomalies during canary.
- Postmortem owner: the squad that promoted the artifact.

Appendix A — Example table: acceptance thresholds
| Metric | GREEN threshold | AMBER threshold | Action when breached |
| Response similarity (p95) | delta <= 1.5% | delta <= 3.5% | AMBER -> manual review; RED -> block |
| Functioncall OK rate | >= 99% | >= 97% | RED if < 97% |
| Safety high-severity hits | 0 | <= 2 isolated low-sev | SEV1 immediate if >0 high-sev |
| Latency p99 | <= baseline * 1.15 | <= baseline * 1.40 | Capacity/rollback plan required |

Appendix B — Minimal replay-output file layout (retain):
- summary.json (top-level metrics)
- diffs/ (per-probe text diffs)
- funcalls/ (json blobs for functioncall traces)
- latency-profile.csv
- token-divergence-histogram.pb (protobuf)

FAQ (short):
Q: Can GREEN stamps be overridden?
A: Yes, Security or Product may veto promotion if additional business constraints apply. Override must be documented in the artifact manifest signer field.

Q: How often should probe bundles be refreshed?
A: Quarterly for core slices, monthly for risk slices with active drift.

Related reading and links:
- Quant profile synthesis guide (internal)
- Quantized artifact eval gate and rollout (internal)
- Probe bundle assembly CLI reference

If you are onboarding a new model family, follow this manual and file a promotion PR with replay-output attached. For questions or exceptions, ping quant-eval in Slack or the reviewers listed above.
